The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the asymptotic case, variable importances in an ensemble of totally-randomized trees are a measure of the information provided by a variable about the output and that this information is independent of the information provided about the output by irrelevant variables.

the MDI importances derived from an ensemble of totally random trees are well-defined, stable with respect to the addition/removal of irrelevant variables, and can be decomposed into a linear combination of the information provided by all input variable pairs, triples, quadruples, etc.
the MDI variable importances of a totally randomized forest can be understood as a measure of the relevance of a given variable in the sense of the information-theoretic notion of irrelevance.
